title: Customs Agent Licensing and Operational Jurisdiction
summary: The regulatory framework for Customs Agent licensing evolved from basic authorization to a structured system involving NBR approval, specific jurisdictional licensing, and formal renewal procedures. Over time, the role of the Customs House shifted from a simple administrative office to a central hub for licensing, oversight, and the management of agent conduct.

evolution.structure: Moved from general authorization to a rigid, jurisdiction-specific licensing model.
evolution.oversight: Increased NBR involvement in vetting and approving new licenses.

timeline.change: Introduced formal procedures for licensing in multiple Customs Houses and established a renewal process for listed licenses.
Formalized the composition of the Licensing Authority within the Customs House and mandated NBR prior approval for new licenses.
Clarified that licenses are strictly tied to the jurisdiction of the specific Customs House or station.

Customs House Licensing: Licensees wishing to operate at a customs station or customs house other than the one specified in their original license must submit a formal application to the respective licensing authority.

The application requires the submission of a specified fee paid via treasury challan, bank draft, or pay order, and the licensing authority will evaluate the applicant's eligibility for inclusion in a list for that location.
Upon approval, the licensee will be registered for the additional customs house or station for the remaining duration of the original license, subject to the prescribed application form.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for verifying applications from licensees who wish to operate at secondary customs stations and for registering them accordingly.

Customs Licensing Authority: The licensing authority at a Customs House or Customs Station is empowered to process and grant renewal applications for listed licenses.
The authority exercises discretion to renew a listed license for a duration equivalent to the validity period of the primary license.
Listed License: The renewal process for a listed license requires the license holder to submit a formal application along with the renewal copy of the primary license.
Applicants must pay a specified renewal fee and the applicable Value Added Tax through treasury challan, bank draft, or pay order to finalize the renewal process.
Value Added Tax: Value Added Tax must be paid on the prescribed renewal fee as part of the financial requirements for renewing a listed license.

Customs Act 1969: This law is defined as the Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) for the purposes of these rules.
Customs Agent: A Customs Agent is defined as a person or institution performing tasks related to the import or export of goods or baggage, or the entry or exit of vehicles at a customs station, as per the objectives of section 207 of the Customs Act.
Customs Government: This term refers to the customs authority or official appointed under rule 17 of these regulations.
Customs Station: This refers to the definition of a customs station as specified in section 2(k) of the Customs Act.
Customs House: This refers to a custom house declared according to section 9(e) of the Customs Act.
Company: This refers to a company as defined in section 2(d) of the Companies Act, 1994.
Customer: This refers to a person or institution that imports goods from abroad or exports goods to a foreign country.
Form: This refers to the forms annexed to these rules for official use.
Firm: This refers to a firm as defined in section 4 of the Partnership Act, 1932.
National Board of Revenue: The term Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue, as specified in section 2(e) of the Customs Act.
Reference License: This refers to a license granted under the provisions of rule 11 of these regulations.
Licensee: This refers to a license granted under rule 5 which authorizes an entity to function as a Customs Agent.
Licensing Authority: This refers to the authority constituted under rule 3 for the purposes of managing and issuing customs agent licenses.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the authority responsible for granting prior approval for the issuance of new licenses.
Upon receiving a written application, the Board evaluates the necessity of new licenses based on existing license counts and recent trade statistics before granting permission to the customs house.
Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority must submit a formal written application to the National Board of Revenue before issuing any new licenses.
This application must include justification for the new license, the current number of active licenses at the customs station, and trade statistics from the previous five years.
Customs House: The Customs House receives the authority to grant new licenses only after the National Board of Revenue has reviewed the application and provided formal permission.

Customs Act 1969: This law is formally referred to as the Act within these rules, establishing the legal framework for customs administration in Bangladesh.
Customs Agent: A customs agent is defined as any person or organization that performs tasks related to the entry or exit of vehicles, or the import or export of goods and baggage at a customs station, as intended under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Broker: Refers to the formal role defined under these rules, which governs those authorized to handle customs-related documentation and procedures on behalf of others.
Customs Station: A customs station is defined in accordance with the specific definition provided under the Customs Act 1969.
Customs House: A custom house is defined as an facility declared and authorized under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969.
Company: Refers to a business entity as defined under the specific section of the Companies Act 1994.
Importer and Exporter: Defined as a person or institution involved in the importation of goods from abroad or the exportation of goods to other countries.
Form: Refers to the official documents appended to these rules that must be utilized for procedural compliance.
Partnership Act 1932: This Act provides the legal definition for a firm for the purposes of these licensing rules.
National Board of Revenue: Identified as the Board within these rules, as defined under the Customs Act 1969.
Reference License: A license issued under the specific rule of this framework to provide authorization for designated customs-related activities.
Licensee: Authorization granted under these rules to an entity enabling them to operate as a customs agent.
Licensing Authority: The body constituted under these rules responsible for the issuance and oversight of customs agent licenses.

Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority is responsible for the issuance of Customs Agent licenses.

The composition of the Licensing Authority is structured based on the available customs officers at the customs house, consisting of a combination of either an Additional Commissioner and a Deputy Commissioner or a Joint Commissioner and an Assistant Commissioner.
The Licensing Authority functions with the senior officer serving as the chairperson and the junior officer serving as the member-secretary.
Customs Agent License: A license required for the operation of customs agents is issued by the designated Licensing Authority.
Customs House: The Customs House serves as the administrative location where the Licensing Authority is constituted and operates from.

Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016: This set of rules establishes the regulatory framework for granting, renewing, suspending, or cancelling licenses for clearing, forwarding, and shipping agents. It mandates the specific form and procedural requirements under which these operations must be conducted at customs houses or customs stations.
Customs Act 1969: Section 207 of this Act provides the primary legal authority for the licensing and regulation of customs agents in Bangladesh.
Customs Agent License: This license is issued under the authority of the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016 for conducting clearing, forwarding, and shipping agency business at a designated customs house or station.
The license is non-transferable and remains valid for a fixed duration of five years from the date of issue, provided it is not cancelled, suspended, or denied renewal for regulatory violations.

Customs Act 1969: Section 207 of this Act provides the primary legal authority for the issuance of customs agent licenses.
Customs Agent License: This license authorizes a person or entity to conduct clearing, forwarding, and shipping business at a specified customs house or station.
The license is non-transferable and remains valid for a set number of years from the date of issuance, provided it is not cancelled, suspended, or denied renewal under the relevant rules.
The scope of the license is geographically limited to the specific customs house or customs station indicated on the document.
Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016: Rule 5(7) of these rules governs the issuance, regulatory framework, and validity period of customs agent licenses.
